concepts.title: Newton's First Law of Motion
concepts.definition: A body keeps doing what it is doing - staying at rest or moving uniformly in a straight line - until a net external force makes it change.
concepts.key_idea: Objects have inertia, resisting changes to their state of motion.
question_patterns: explain why a passenger jerks forward when a bus stops
what happens to an object if the net external force is zero
define the law of inertia
identify the state of motion when forces are balanced
what do you understand by newton's first law of motion

solution_steps.explain: List all forces acting on the body from the environment.
Sum the force vectors to check if they cancel out.
If the net force is zero, the body remains at rest or in uniform motion, confirming the first law.

concepts.title: Linear Momentum
concepts.definition: The vector quantity representing the product of an object's mass and its instantaneous velocity.
concepts.key_idea: Momentum quantifies the 'amount of motion' and varies with both mass and speed.
question_patterns: calculate the momentum of a body
find the product of mass and velocity
what is the momentum of a mass m moving at speed v
how much momentum does a vehicle have
work out the value using linear momentum

solution_steps.explain: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity.
Momentum is a vector, so its direction is the same as the velocity vector.
If velocity changes, the change in momentum is mass times the change in velocity.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving linear momentum.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: multiply mass and velocity. Step 2: determine direction of momentum. Step 3: compute change in momentum. Working: mass * velocity, mass * (v_final - v_initial).
worked_examples.answer: Linear Momentum applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply linear momentum to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: multiply mass and velocity. Step 2: determine direction of momentum. Step 3: compute change in momentum. Working: mass * velocity, mass * (v_final - v_initial).
worked_examples.answer: The method of linear momentum leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Newton's Second Law of Motion
concepts.definition: The net force acting on a body equals the result of multiplying its mass and the acceleration produced.
concepts.key_idea: Force is indeed the rate of change of momentum over time.
question_patterns: calculate the force required to accelerate a mass
find the acceleration of a body under a given force
what is the net force acting on the object
determine the mass if force and acceleration are known
solve a numerical on newton's second law of motion

solution_steps.explain: Force is calculated as mass times acceleration.

solution_steps.action: compute rate of change of momentum
solution_steps.explain: Force equals the change in momentum divided by the time interval over which it changes.
The net force acts in the same direction as the acceleration produced.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving newton's second law of motion.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: multiply mass by acceleration. Step 2: compute rate of change of momentum. Step 3: determine direction of force. Working: mass * acceleration, (mass * (v_final - v_initial)) / time.
worked_examples.answer: Newton's Second Law of Motion applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply newton's second law of motion to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: multiply mass by acceleration. Step 2: compute rate of change of momentum. Step 3: determine direction of force. Working: mass * acceleration, (mass * (v_final - v_initial)) / time.
worked_examples.answer: The method of newton's second law of motion leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Impulse
concepts.definition: The product of a large force and the short time interval during which it acts, resulting in a change in momentum.
concepts.key_idea: Impulse measures the total change in momentum brought about by a force.
question_patterns: calculate the impulse imparted to a ball
find the change in momentum
what is the product of force and time
determine the impulse from mass and velocity change
work out the value using impulse

solution_steps.explain: Find the difference between final and initial velocity.
Impulse equals the change in momentum.
Divide the impulse by the contact time to obtain the average force applied during the collision.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving impulse.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate velocity change. Step 2: multiply mass by velocity change. Step 3: compute average force. Working: v_final - v_initial, mass * delta_v, impulse / time_duration.
worked_examples.answer: Impulse applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply impulse to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate velocity change. Step 2: multiply mass by velocity change. Step 3: compute average force. Working: v_final - v_initial, mass * delta_v, impulse / time_duration.
worked_examples.answer: The method of impulse leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Newton's Third Law of Motion
concepts.definition: Whenever two bodies interact, the force applied by the first on the second is equal in both magnitude and opposite in direction to the force applied by the second on the first.
concepts.key_idea: Forces always exist in pairs acting on different bodies.
question_patterns: state the law of action and reaction
identify the reaction force to a given action
why do action and reaction forces not cancel each other
explain how a swimmer pushes the water
explain newton's third law of motion in your own words

solution_steps.explain: Determine the two objects exerting forces on each other.
Force on A by B is equal and opposite to force on B by A.

solution_steps.action: confirm forces act on different bodies
solution_steps.explain: Since the action and reaction forces act on different bodies, they do not cancel each other and cannot be summed as a single net force.

concepts.title: Law of Conservation of Momentum
concepts.definition: The total linear momentum of an isolated system remains constant if no external force acts on it.
concepts.key_idea: Internal forces cannot change the total momentum of a system.
question_patterns: find the recoil velocity of a gun
calculate the final velocity after a collision
what is the total momentum of the system
determine the mass of an object using momentum conservation
work out the value using law of conservation of momentum

solution_steps.explain: Sum the momenta of all parts before the interaction.
Total momentum is conserved, so p_final = p_initial.
Check that the sum of final momenta equals the initial total momentum to confirm conservation.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving law of conservation of momentum.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate initial total momentum. Step 2: equate to final momentum. Step 3: verify total final momentum. Working: m1 * u1 + m2 * u2, (p_initial - m1 * v1) / m2, m1 * v1 + m2 * v2.
worked_examples.answer: Law of Conservation of Momentum applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply law of conservation of momentum to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate initial total momentum. Step 2: equate to final momentum. Step 3: verify total final momentum. Working: m1 * u1 + m2 * u2, (p_initial - m1 * v1) / m2, m1 * v1 + m2 * v2.
worked_examples.answer: The method of law of conservation of momentum leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Static Friction
concepts.definition: The friction that must be overcome before one surface starts sliding over another.
concepts.key_idea: Static friction is self-adjusting up to a maximum limiting value.
question_patterns: calculate the maximum static frictional force
find the coefficient of static friction
what is the limiting friction
determine if a block will slide given an applied force
work out the value using static friction

solution_steps.explain: On a level surface, normal force equals weight.
Limiting friction is the product of coefficient and normal force.

solution_steps.action: compare applied force with limiting friction
solution_steps.explain: If the applied force exceeds the limiting friction, the body begins to slide; otherwise it remains at rest.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving static friction.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate normal force. Step 2: multiply by coefficient. Step 3: compare applied force with limiting friction. Working: mass * 9.8, mu_s * normal_force.
worked_examples.answer: Static Friction applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply static friction to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate normal force. Step 2: multiply by coefficient. Step 3: compare applied force with limiting friction. Working: mass * 9.8, mu_s * normal_force.
worked_examples.answer: The method of static friction leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Kinetic Friction
concepts.definition: The frictional force acting between surfaces that are in relative motion.
concepts.key_idea: Kinetic friction is indeed generally less than the maximum static friction.
question_patterns: calculate the kinetic frictional force
find the acceleration of a sliding block
what is the resistive force during motion
determine the coefficient of kinetic friction
what is the result in this kinetic friction problem

solution_steps.explain: Normal force is mass times gravity on a level plane.
Kinetic friction is coefficient times normal force.
The net deceleration of the sliding body is kinetic friction divided by mass.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving kinetic friction.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate normal force. Step 2: calculate friction. Step 3: compute net acceleration. Working: mass * 9.8, mu_k * normal_force, f_k / mass.
worked_examples.answer: Kinetic Friction applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply kinetic friction to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate normal force. Step 2: calculate friction. Step 3: compute net acceleration. Working: mass * 9.8, mu_k * normal_force, f_k / mass.
worked_examples.answer: The method of kinetic friction leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Centripetal Force
concepts.definition: The center-directed force required to maintain an object's uniform circular motion.
concepts.key_idea: Centripetal force is not a new type of force but a requirement for circular paths.
question_patterns: calculate the centripetal force on a car
find the tension in a whirling string
what force keeps a planet in orbit
determine the force needed for a turn of radius r
solve a numerical on centripetal force

solution_steps.explain: The formula requires velocity squared.
Force is mass times velocity squared divided by radius.
Divide the centripetal force by mass to obtain the inward radial acceleration.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving centripetal force.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: square the velocity. Step 2: calculate force. Step 3: compute centripetal acceleration. Working: velocity * velocity, mass * v_sq / radius, force / mass.
worked_examples.answer: Centripetal Force applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply centripetal force to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: square the velocity. Step 2: calculate force. Step 3: compute centripetal acceleration. Working: velocity * velocity, mass * v_sq / radius, force / mass.
worked_examples.answer: The method of centripetal force leads to the required value or conclusion.

concepts.title: Max Speed on Level Road
concepts.definition: The maximum velocity a vehicle can achieve on a flat circular track without skidding.
concepts.key_idea: Friction provides the necessary centripetal force on a level road.
question_patterns: find the maximum speed of a car on a turn
will the cyclist slip at this speed
calculate the safe speed for a radius r
what is the limit of velocity on a flat road
what is the result in this max speed on level road problem

solution_steps.action: calculate product of mu, r, and g
solution_steps.explain: The square of max velocity depends on friction, radius, and gravity.
The maximum speed is the square root of the product.
At the maximum speed, friction supplies exactly the centripetal force needed for the turn.

worked_examples.question: Solve a typical question involving max speed on level road.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate product of mu, r, and g. Step 2: take square root. Step 3: compute required centripetal force. Working: mu_s * radius * 9.8, sqrt(v_sq), mass * (v_max**2) / radius.
worked_examples.answer: Max Speed on Level Road applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.question: Apply max speed on level road to a fresh example and interpret the result.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: calculate product of mu, r, and g. Step 2: take square root. Step 3: compute required centripetal force. Working: mu_s * radius * 9.8, sqrt(v_sq), mass * (v_max**2) / radius.
worked_examples.answer: The method of max speed on level road leads to the required value or conclusion.
